projects.title: First Rust programs
projects.description: Four small programs: a greeting that reads a name, then three functions that calculate with i32 and f64 values.

tasks.title: Greet someone by name
tasks.prompt:
The starter reads one line of input into `name` and trims the line break. Print exactly one line: `Hello, NAME! Welcome to Rust.` with the name in place of NAME.

If the input is `Ada`, the program prints `Hello, Ada! Welcome to Rust.`
hints: println! can print a variable by name inside the braces: `{name}`.
The whole line is `println!("Hello, {name}! Welcome to Rust.");`
tasks.correction: Compare your output with the expected line character by character. The comma, the exclamation mark and the full stop all count.
tasks.explanation: `let name = name.trim();` shadows the original `name` with the trimmed text, so the greeting has no stray line break. `{name}` inside the braces prints it.

cases.expected: Hello, Grace Hopper! Welcome to Rust.

tasks.title: Area of a rectangle
tasks.prompt:
Write a function `area` that returns the area of a rectangle. The width, the height and the result are all `i32` values.

The checker calls `area` for you, so this file needs no `fn main`. Run shows what your function returns for the example.
hints: The area is width multiplied by height.
Make `width * height` the last line of the body, with no semicolon.
tasks.correction: Check that the last line of the body is `width * height` with no semicolon after it. A semicolon would make the function return nothing.
tasks.explanation: The body's last expression is the return value, so `width * height` with no semicolon is returned as the `i32` the signature promises.

tasks.title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
tasks.prompt:
Write `to_fahrenheit`, which takes a temperature in Celsius as an `f64` and returns it in Fahrenheit as an `f64`.

To convert, multiply by 9, divide by 5 and add 32. Every number in the calculation needs to be an `f64`, so write `9.0` rather than `9`.
hints: Rust won't multiply an f64 by the integer 9. Write the constants as 9.0, 5.0 and 32.0.
tasks.correction: Check the order: multiply by 9.0, divide by 5.0, then add 32.0. Then check that the result is the last expression of the body, with no semicolon.
tasks.explanation: Every value in `celsius * 9.0 / 5.0 + 32.0` is an `f64`, so Rust needs no conversion. Multiplication and division happen before the addition.

tasks.title: Average of three scores
tasks.prompt:
Write `average`, which takes three `i32` scores and returns their average as an `f64`.

The sum of three `i32` values is an `i32`. Convert it with `as f64` before dividing, or the remainder is lost.
hints: Add the three scores first. That sum is an i32.
`(a + b + c) as f64` gives you an f64. Divide it by 3.0.
tasks.correction: If you get a whole-number answer, the division happened between two i32 values. Convert the sum to f64 before dividing, and divide by 3.0.
tasks.explanation: `(a + b + c) as f64` converts the sum, then dividing by `3.0` keeps the fraction. Dividing first, with `(a + b + c) / 3`, would drop it.
